executiveSummary: GM0321's 2025 identity, centre, population, 61 neighbourhoods, eleven districts, four BAG places, eleven settlement labels, two railway stations and five road-border links are internally coherent. The annual municipality control of 50,945 residents differs by twenty (+0.039%) from rounded neighbourhood rows and is correctly reconciled without rewriting observations. The complete deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint and eight-service contract passes. Release is nevertheless correction-required. The generic river preset reaches exactly 1.549453 m by T+12 and holds that municipality-wide value unchanged through T+72, with 29,460 affected resident-equivalents and 1,936,447.991 deprived person-hours at T+72, without selecting a Lek level, dike segment/state, breach, connected footprint, probability, arrival or recession. Official local evidence instead describes a particular Wijk bij Duurstede–Amerongen breach case: much of Houten at 0.5–1.5 m, Eiland van Schalkwijk up to 5 m, core arrival within 24 hours, partly inundated A12/A27 evacuation routes and water lasting weeks or longer. Eight active T+24 presets reuse the same neighbourhood ranking. The generic pluvial result consumes neither Houten's current 30 cm stress-test surface nor named sewer/tunnel/wadi risks, and the municipality publishes materially different T=100 risk-location totals for older and current model editions. Road-only mobility/supply links omit rail and flood-valid local access, while care referral, utilities, wastewater, communications and incident-time occupancy remain synthetic or Unknown. Public data can constrain the first 72 hours, but no register, plan or point observation establishes live defence, asset, route, facility or restoration state. Unknown and NoData must never be shown as zero or safe.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM0321 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, place and settlement geography and statistics
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026; full CBS feature retrieved 3 September 2026
supports: Annual CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK input identifies GM0321 as Houten in Utrecht and reports 50,945 residents, density 928/km², 19.6% aged 65 or older and 6,262 one-person households; the generated centre [5.195465840469772,51.999864800541694] lies inside the 2025 boundary.

Sixty-one neighbourhood rows in eleven districts sum to 50,965 residents, twenty above the municipality total (+0.039%); households sum to 21,320 and independently rounded age-65-plus rows to 9,990. Allocation reconciles to 50,945 without rewriting source observations.

BAG supplies four active woonplaatsen—'t Goy, Houten, Schalkwijk and Tull en 't Waal—and BRT supplies eleven labels: four woonkernen, four buurtschappen and three deelkernen. No place centre falls outside the generalized boundary. BAG/PDOK is Public Domain Mark 1.0 and CBS/BRT is CC BY 4.0.

The generated overview MultiPolygon has 71 coordinate positions versus 1,966 in the fresh non-generalized feature. Cars-per-household covers 43/61 neighbourhoods, home/value and several benefits 48/61, doctor/supermarket distance 50/61, while district heat and charging cover 0/61; null and suppressed values remain NoData.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Climate Adaptation Plan 2022–2027, current extreme-rain study and Water and Sewerage Plan 2024–2027
evidenceSources.edition: Climate Adaptation Plan December 2022; WRP 2024–2027 adopted December 2023; current municipal pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The adopted 2022 plan identifies urban waterlogging and hard-surface heat as Houten's largest climate threats. Its older T=100 calculation (93 mm/85 minutes) reported 345 risk locations and 1,283 buildings, named tunnel, wadi and street trouble spots, and found Houten centre/Castellum heat stress with many older residents.

The municipality's current rain page reports a 30×30 cm climate calculation for the same T=100 93 mm/85-minute event with 453 locations above the >10 cm-at-façade risk criterion; it also reports 101 T=10 and 166 T=50 locations and work at 58 locations/approximately 215 buildings. The page does not expose a downloadable raster, model edition/date, change log, uncertainty, NoData or standard reuse licence, so its counts must not be merged with the older edition.

The WRP 2024–2027 covers wastewater, rain, groundwater and surface water, requires at least 40 mm private-site retention for building plans, planned a 2025 recalculation/stress test, and notes that a sudden business discharge can disrupt pressure sewerage. It is adopted policy/design context, not a live sewer, pump or capacity feed.

The 2022 flood case states that after a Lekdijk breach between Wijk bij Duurstede and Amerongen, part of 't Goy and small eastern areas remain dry, much of Houten reaches 0.5–1.5 m, low Eiland van Schalkwijk can reach 5 m, the urban core can be reached within 24 hours, A12/A27 evacuation routes partly flood, and water can remain for weeks. These are a dated scenario study, not current probability, depth or evacuation order.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Sterke Lekdijk Culemborgse Veer–Beatrixsluis safety project
evidenceSources.edition: Definitive project decision published 2025; current plan-development/project pages inspected 3 September 2026; works expected 2027–2029
supports: The eleven-kilometre project runs from Culemborgse Veer to Prinses Beatrixsluis; about five kilometres between Beatrixsluis and Fort Honswijk require strengthening, with a local height task and broader piping and inward-macrostability tasks.

The definitive project decision and planned works establish a bounded safety project, not a current failure, breach probability, present strength, water level or operational restriction. Dryness inspections and cable/pipe investigations in 2026 likewise remain dated project observations.

HDSR states that the northern Lekdijk protects more than one million people who live and work in west/central Netherlands. This supports cross-boundary consequence and coordination, not an exposed-person count for a selected event.

The public project pages/documents provide segment and project-phase evidence but no standard machine event cadence or standard redistribution licence identified. Current defence state, breach, local inundation, access and recovery remain Unknown without an authority-selected event.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2023 and Regionaal Crisisplan 2024–2027
evidenceSources.edition: Regional risk profile 2023; regional crisis plan 2024–2027
supports: VRU treats river flooding as catastrophic and a single Lekdijk breach near Amerongen as the regional reference event; it highlights continuity of assistance, scarcity of people/resources and the potential need for additional capacity and large-scale evacuation.

The risk profile separates extreme rain, storm, heat/drought, nature fire, vital-infrastructure disruption and cyber dependence. It says electricity/vital-process loss can cause national road, water and rail transport knock-on effects and that cyber disruption of water, drinking-water or energy systems is a vital-infrastructure event.

The crisis plan distinguishes acute flash crises, flexibly scaled foreseeable storm/flood events and prolonged project-like crises such as drought. This supports different action clocks rather than one generic response curve.

The PDFs are public regional governance/risk evidence with dated editions, no machine incident cadence and no standard redistribution licence identified. They do not provide current event probability, staff/resource availability, dispatch, evacuation decision or restoration commitments.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — LIWO 2025 breach-candidate and Waterinfo Lek point context
evidenceSources.edition: LIWO release 2025.1.6; Waterinfo snapshots retrieved 2–3 September 2026
supports: LIWO is professional flood-preparedness information requiring specialist water-manager interpretation. Exact containment against the full 2025 Houten boundary finds one primary candidate, Wijk bij Duurstede–A27 [5.1602,51.9797], and zero points in the regional, regional-water-system and outer-dike candidate categories. The point is an entry for finding scenarios, not an active breach or selected footprint.

Empty candidate categories are no matches in those releases/queries, not zero local-water, outer-dike or flood risk. Any scenario adapter must preserve release, source, defence/breach case, probability band, unit/datum, cell, coverage, NoData and licence.

The deployed Waterinfo snapshot assigns the Culemborg water-level point to GM0321: 221 cm NAP at 17:30Z on 2 September 2026. Forecast snapshots give 223, 223, 224 and 226 cm NAP at requested T+1/6/12/24; no Culemborg point remains at T+48 and the national public endpoint returns no T+72 water-level features.

Waterinfo is generally CC0, commonly ten-minute observations and a public non-mission-critical point service; its frontend forecast endpoint is not a stable external API contract. These point values are neither dike state nor inundation depth and cannot be silently aligned to a synthetic event; absent T+48/T+72 is NoData, not zero.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — NWB road gateways, rail stations, scheduled transit and timestamped situation context
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light 1 August 2026; ProRail/GTFS/NDW deployment snapshots retrieved 31 August–2 September 2026
supports: The monthly CC0 NWB graph has five mobility/supply-only border links: A27 north to Utrecht and west/south to Nieuwegein, N421/N410 to Bunnik and N409 to Nieuwegein. The two A27 edges are one physical corridor and nominal 260/150 values are non-additive scenario units, not measured emergency capacity.

The CC0 ProRail register places Houten and Houten Castellum stations inside the boundary. OVapi GTFS version 9543, retrieved 31 August and valid 30 August–12 December 2026 under free-use/best-effort/no-SLA terms, supplies 98 in-boundary stop areas; schedules/geometry are not service, passenger counts, accessibility or disruption state.

The dated climate case says A12/A27 evacuation routes can partly flood, while the logical network has no selected flood/passability/evacuation direction or rail dependency. Local tunnel, round-road and village access also remain outside the causal graph.

The CC0-unless-stated NDW snapshot contains a nearest real record about 3.09 km from the municipality reference point, with event type 'other' and unknown severity at retrieval. A nearby record does not identify Houten route passability; an absent matching route state is Unknown rather than open.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Stichting Mijn Aansluiting / Netbeheer Nederland
evidenceSources.title: E07 — Public water-asset, provider-responsibility and electricity-planning context
evidenceSources.edition: Public/deployment snapshots retrieved 31 August–3 September 2026; provider timestamps 7 September 2025–24 March 2026
supports: The partial HWH spatial assignment contains 232 GM0321 objects: 208 weirs, eighteen surface-water pumps, five sewer pumps and one wastewater treatment plant. HWH Kunstwerken is national/weekly and Waterketen DAMO contributor-dependent, both CC BY-SA 4.0; points are not validated connectivity, units, live state, capacity or backup.

Public Domain Mijn Aansluiting WMS/WFS identifies Stedin electricity (updated 24 March 2026), Stedin gas (17 December 2025), Vitens drinking water and Ziggo media (both 7 September 2025) at the municipality reference point and returns no drainage polygon. Provider territory is responsibility context, not physical topology, outage or restoration; empty drainage remains Unknown.

One NBNL postcode sample at 3998KA maps to Stedin service area Nieuwegein and reports 48.8 MW withdrawal queue/91 requests, 200/196.9 MW existing/required injection, 13.4 MW injection queue/46 requests, 29 projects and earliest year 2030; withdrawal capacity values are null.

NBNL planning/queue data updates at least quarterly/monthly with no exact standard licence identifier found and is neither complete municipality coverage nor live load, spare emergency capacity, switching, outage or restoration. Null existing/required withdrawal values remain Unknown.

evidenceSources.publisher: RDI / DUO / RIVM / KNMI / IPO Risicokaart
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Public communications, education, acute-care, weather, air, seismic and nature-fire context
evidenceSources.edition: Public/deployment snapshots retrieved 31 August–3 September 2026; RIVM acute-care v1.1 published 3 July 2026; Risicokaart metadata updated 19 February 2026
supports: RDI assigns eighty antenna installations—36 mobile, twenty fixed-link, 21 amateur, two broadcast and one other-mobile—and daily attribution-licensed DUO data assigns 48 education locations: 23 primary, three secondary, two vocational/adult, one special and nineteen other registered. Registers do not establish coverage, occupancy, shelter role, backup or operation; RDI licence/cadence is unstated.

RIVM acute-care v1.1 CC0 has no point in GM0321. St. Antonius Nieuwegein is nearest to the reference point at 8.32 km straight-line and reports a 24/7 emergency department, eighteen treatment rooms and 22,094 visits in 2025; this is questionnaire context, not route time, diversion, staffing, occupancy or guaranteed capacity.

No KNMI station lies inside; De Bilt is nearest at 11.06 km in the retrieved ten-minute CC BY 4.0 observation snapshot. No RIVM PM2.5 point lies inside; Utrecht-Griftpark is nearest at 12.18 km. No seismic event origin lies inside the 365-day CC BY 4.0 KNMI query; the nearest is an induced M1.72 Noordbeemster origin 65.76 km away. No-match is not zero local weather, air exposure or seismic hazard.

The Public Domain Risicokaart combustible-nature query returns no feature intersecting the full Houten polygon; the large Utrechtse Heuvelrug polygon is outside. This is layer coverage/eligibility context, not proof of no local vegetation, ignition, smoke, fuel moisture or nature-fire risk.

identity.summary: GM0321, Houten, Utrecht and safety region Utrecht agree across generated and official 2025 inputs.
notes: Feature id, bundle code/name, province, safety-region membership and 2025 boundary/statistics editions agree.
The municipality reference point lies inside the generalized and full boundaries.
No identity, province, safety-region or headline-population contradiction was found.

geography.summary: Administrative geography is coherent, but analytical flood, asset and route work requires the full boundary and physical surfaces.
notes: The 71-position overview and 1,966-position full CBS feature are both MultiPolygons; the overview is appropriate for display, not hydraulic, defence, waterbody, asset or route intersection.
No BAG place-centre mismatch is present, and all 61 neighbourhood rows carry GM0321.
Lek floodplain, Eiland van Schalkwijk, Amsterdam-Rijnkanaal, dike segments, local drainage, tunnels, roads and buildings cannot be inferred from administrative centres.

demography.summary: Official 2025 municipality controls and neighbourhood rows reconcile within CBS rounding/publication precision.
notes: Official/generated population is 50,945, density 928/km², age 65+ is 19.6% and one-person households number 6,262.
Neighbourhood rows sum to 50,965 (+20, +0.039%); households sum to 21,320 and rounded age-65-plus rows to 9,990.
Registered residents are not incident-time workers, pupils, patients, rail/transit users, visitors, responders or displaced people.

regionalDetail.summary: Neighbourhood detail is strong, but source sparsity and incompatible rain-study editions require explicit NoData and version semantics.
notes: All 61 rows provide population, age, household, business, buildings and land/water fields; several housing/access fields cover 43–50 rows and heating/charging cover zero. Null is not imputed.
The adopted climate plan's 345 T=100 locations and current page's 453 are distinct calculation editions. The current page lacks downloadable raster/version metadata needed for causal ingestion.
HWH objects, provider areas, the NBNL sample, schools, antennas, care and monitoring points remain source-bounded context with affectsSimulation=false.

settlements.summary: Four BAG places and eleven BRT labels coherently represent the urban core and smaller rural settlements.
notes: BAG contains 't Goy, Houten, Schalkwijk and Tull en 't Waal; all four place centres lie inside the generalized boundary.
BRT adds descriptive labels including Honswijk, Heemstede, Oud-Wulven and smaller localities.
Labels do not establish occupancy, vulnerability, evacuation zones, catchments, service continuity or hazard footprint.

transport.summary: Five road reference links and two stations are present, but flood-valid evacuation, rail and local access are not causal.
notes: NWB supplies A27, N421, N409 and N410 mobility/supply-only links toward Utrecht, Nieuwegein and Bunnik; the two A27 records are one non-additive physical corridor.

The local flood case says A12/A27 routes partly inundate and water reaches the core within 24 hours, yet no breach-specific road cell, closure direction, evacuation load, destination or timing alters mobility.
Houten/Houten Castellum stations and 98 GTFS stop areas remain static reference context; rail, bus, local tunnel and cross-canal/care transfers have no operational state.
A timestamped NDW record or absence of a matched situation does not prove any route open through T+72.

emergencyContext.summary: Strong first-72-hour flood, weather, lifeline and preparedness context exists, but no selected event or live response state is consumed.
notes: Local/regional evidence supports a foreseeable Lek flood with pre-impact evacuation, urban/rural rain differences, heat-vulnerable older residents, prolonged disruption, resource scarcity and vital-service cascades.
Waterinfo/KNMI/NDW/air records retain observation/valid time and limited point/record coverage and cannot be projected across synthetic scenario time.

Defence projects, stress tests, asset/provider registers, congestion planning, schools, antennas and care questionnaire are planning/register context, not current readiness, occupancy or availability.
Defence/pump/sewer state, evacuation decision, road/rail passability, care capacity, utility topology, backup, staffing, resources and restoration remain Unknown or explicitly synthetic.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten canonical scenarios execute at all six mandatory checkpoints for all eight services.
notes: Initial MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM0321 pnpm audit:model passed two tests covering ten presets, T+0/6/12/24/48/72 and power/water/drainage/gas/telecom/mobility/facilities/supply.
Focused reproductions captured all preset T+24/T+72 municipality, service and 61-neighbourhood values and the full river six-checkpoint trajectory without creating a repository test file.
Coastal T+24 has zero direct depth and zero affected residents but wind-related system pressure; wildfire is a remote-smoke/drought exercise and earthquake/cyber have no selected local event/target.
Outputs are deterministic exercise indices/resident-equivalents, not observations, probabilities, casualties, measured water depth or operator commitments.

numericalInvariants.summary: Determinism, finite bounds, exact no-event behavior, allocation, reconciliation and cumulative burden pass.
notes: All service availability remains in [0,1]; hazard, demand, delivery, affected residents and deprived person-hours remain finite and non-negative.
Zero-intensity scenarios return exact zero event hazard, affected population and attributable burden; repeated runs are deterministic and burden is monotone.
Every service allocates all 61 neighbourhoods and reconciles to 50,945 residents; local demand/delivery closes to municipality totals and layer selection does not mutate the scenario.
Passing arithmetic does not validate hydraulic depth, spatial allocation, evacuation feasibility, incident occupancy, utility topology or restoration precision.

spatialPlausibility.summary: A source-free river scalar and common neighbourhood seed ignore the selected-breach, terrain, rain, heat and access evidence.
notes: River depth rises from zero at T+0 to 0.545407 m at T+6 and 1.549453 m at T+12, then remains identical through T+72 without a selected Lek level, defence/breach, connected raster, arrival or recession.

Storm, pluvial, river, coastal/wind, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire at T+24 share the exact leading order Grassen, Buitengebied Schalkwijk West, Hagen, Sporen and Weiden; compound converges to it at T+72.

The dated local breach case distinguishes partly dry 't Goy, 0.5–1.5 m over much of Houten and up to 5 m in low Eiland van Schalkwijk. The current rain study supplies a separate 30 cm grid and named building threshold, while heat concentrates around centre/Castellum.

Administrative centres/common seed cannot substitute for selected hydraulic cells, elevation, defences, rain/sewer surface, imperviousness, shade, demographics, source/target or exposed-object geometry.

serviceDependencies.summary: Mobility/supply roads are correctly separated from utilities, but all physical lifelines, rail and care referral remain absent or synthetic.
notes: The five NWB edges support mobility/supply only, avoiding a false utility-road equivalence, but they have no event-valid flood intersection, passability, direction, capacity or destination state.
The 232 HWH objects and municipal sewer evidence do not form a connected surface-water/sewer/pump/RWZI graph or affect drainage/water restoration.

Provider territories and one NBNL sample cannot support exact electricity, water, gas or telecom availability; Houten's two stations, external ED, schools and antennas have no continuity or dependency edges.
Exact T+24/T+72 service values remain transparent synthetic indices pending safe aggregate operator/facility calibration.

causalTrace.summary: Numerical ledgers close, but source version, event selection and accountable first-72-hour actions are outside the graph.
notes: Hazard contributions sum to severity, service contributions reconstruct availability and municipality pressure contributions reconcile exactly.

Current public layers correctly remain affectsSimulation=false. The trace does not select the older/current rain edition, LIWO breach/footprint, defence state, road/rail observation, worker/patient population, facility state or utility topology.

A foreseeable river flood needs a pre-impact phase and separate warning, evacuation, closure, rescue, shelter, care-transfer, dewatering and re-entry decisions; the present scenario begins at T+0 with no event-specific lead-time ledger.
Actions lack accountable owner, trigger, request, decision, resource, dependency, execution, verification and rollback states.

recovery72h.summary: Persistent river disruption is directionally plausible, but exact T+12–72 constancy and recovery consequences are not locally calibrated.
notes: River T+72 retains exactly 1.549453 m, severity 0.484496, pressure 0.550445, 29,460 affected and 1,936,447.991 person-hours; availability ranges from drainage 0.208193 to gas 0.665207 and is unchanged from T+24.

The dated municipal case says water can remain for weeks and the area may take up to a year to become dry, accessible, habitable and liveable, so rapid generic repair would be wrong—but it does not validate a spatially uniform constant model field.

Compound T+72 retains 0.595740 depth/stress, 35,890 affected and 2,118,891.224 person-hours; telecom is 0.223896 and mobility 0.649597. These exact values lack selected water, access, care, crew and operator milestones.

Keep persistent-flood repair blocking as a conservative synthetic guard, but expose uncertainty and do not imply a local restoration promise until dewatering compartments and action-valid recovery curves are selected.

findings.summary: Official 2025 identity, boundary, places and demographic controls reconcile.
findings.evidence: GM0321, Houten, Utrecht and safety region Utrecht agree; the centre and all four BAG place centres are contained. CBS reports 50,945 residents and neighbourhood rows sum to 50,965 (+0.039%).
findings.action: Retain source editions, licence, suppression/null semantics and published-versus-allocated reconciliation without rewriting the twenty-person publication difference.

findings.summary: Sparse statistics and empty public queries remain Unknown rather than false zero or safe state.
findings.evidence: Heating/charging, provider drainage, NBNL withdrawal values, in-boundary acute-care/air/weather/seismic/combustible matches and Culemborg T+48/T+72 forecasts are absent or null in their scoped sources.
findings.action: Keep source coverage, retrieval/effective time, edition, quality, suppression and NoData through ingestion, aggregation, simulation eligibility and UI; distinguish scoped zero from Unknown.

findings.summary: A generic centre-distance scalar emits an unsupported exact 1.549453 m Lek flood through T+72.
findings.evidence: Depth rises to 0.545407 m at T+6 and 1.549453 m at T+12, then remains unchanged through T+72 with 29,460 affected and 1,936,447.991 person-hours. No river level, dike segment/state, breach, probability, connected footprint, arrival or recession is selected; one LIWO candidate is not a selected scenario.
findings.action: Suppress decision-facing depth, exposure and recovery until HDSR/VRU selects a versioned LIWO/LDO case. Retain the proximity scalar only as a non-operational diagnostic and preserve non-selected areas/cells as Unknown, not dry.

findings.summary: The first-24-hour evacuation pathway is missing although official evidence says warning time and routes are limiting.
findings.evidence: The dated local case says water can reach the urban core within 24 hours, current policy is preventive evacuation under threat, and parts of A12/A27 can flood. The scenario begins dry at T+0, reaches modeled water by T+6 and has no warning, decision, population movement, route-cell, destination, shelter, rail, care-transfer or clearance state.
findings.action: Add a pre-impact warning/decision phase and explicit owner-triggered evacuation ledger. Intersect selected arrival cells with A27/A12/N-roads, local tunnels and rail; preserve capacity/passability/destination as Unknown until event-valid authority/operator data is supplied.

findings.summary: Eight unrelated active hazards reuse one neighbourhood ordering.
findings.evidence: Storm, pluvial, river, coastal/wind, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire T+24 all rank Grassen, Buitengebied Schalkwijk West, Hagen, Sporen and Weiden first in that order; compound converges to the same order at T+72.
findings.action: Replace the common seed with hazard-specific physical surfaces and source/target/exposed-object intersections. Preserve deterministic tie-breaking only after evidence-derived values and keep unsupported cells Unknown rather than pseudo-precise.

findings.summary: Older and current municipal T=100 rain results differ materially and the simulator consumes neither version.
findings.evidence: The adopted 2022 plan reports 345 risk locations/1,283 buildings from the older 93 mm/85-minute calculation; the current municipal page reports 453 locations for the same labelled event using a 30 cm grid. No machine raster/version/change log is attached, while the generic pluvial T+24 emits 0.577745 depth/stress and the common ranking.
findings.action: Publish or obtain the governing raster and metadata, store each study as a separate immutable edition and never merge counts. Bind a scenario only after rain hyetograph, sewer/surface-water assumptions, grid, unit, thresholds, mitigation state, uncertainty, NoData and licence are explicit.

findings.summary: Named sewer, pump, surface-water and wastewater evidence is not connected to drainage or recovery.
findings.evidence: The municipality names tunnels, wadis, streets, pressure-sewer constraints and new rain results; HWH assigns 208 weirs, eighteen surface pumps, five sewer pumps and one RWZI. None supplies validated topology/state or affects model water/drainage availability.
findings.action: Add an HDSR/municipality-approved, non-sensitive catchment–surface water–sewer–pump–RWZI graph with event-valid state and backup bands. Treat register status/design limits as context and preserve absent connectivity/capacity as Unknown.

findings.summary: Road-only mobility/supply omits two rail stations, transit, local tunnel failure and event-valid destination access.
findings.evidence: The graph has five NWB links and no rail edge; ProRail has Houten and Houten Castellum and GTFS has 98 stop areas. Official rain/flood evidence identifies the Koppeling tunnel and A12/A27 route vulnerability, but no observation or selected footprint governs access.
findings.action: Add typed, non-additive rail/transit/local-crossing proxies and selected-flood route intersection for mobility and evidenced supply only. Record direction, effective time, validity, accessibility, destination, unit, licence and Unknown live capacity.

findings.summary: Cross-municipal acute-care referral, schools and communications cannot influence first-72-hour prioritisation.
findings.evidence: No RIVM acute-care point is in Houten; nearest questionnaire ED is St. Antonius Nieuwegein 8.32 km straight-line. Forty-eight education sites and eighty antenna installations are context only, and the model has no referral route, vulnerable occupancy, facility role, radio coverage, power/backup or continuity state.
findings.action: Add authorised non-sensitive facility roles, referral catchments, accessibility, communications dependency and time-varying occupancy; compute event-valid travel/isolation and retain staffing, beds, shelter capacity, coverage and backup as Unknown unless supplied.

findings.summary: Zero-resident business districts receive heuristic service demand but cannot represent people present during an incident.
findings.evidence: Schepen, Boten and Vesten each have official zero residents but respectively 90/165/155 businesses and 184/161/98 non-residential buildings. The local allocator retains business/building demand weights, yet affectedPopulation remains zero and worker/visitor counts are unavailable.
findings.action: Keep official resident zero and separate heuristic activity demand from people exposure. Add timestamped worker/visitor counts only from authoritative aggregates; otherwise label occupancy and evacuation demand Unknown and never derive persons from buildings or firms.

findings.summary: Coastal, earthquake, wildfire/smoke and cyber outputs are narrow synthetic exercises rather than local all-clear or forecasts.
findings.evidence: Coastal T+24 direct depth/affected are zero but wind creates pressure; wildfire has zero direct flame/affected with smoke 0.324931; earthquake is zero by T+24 after an earlier generic pulse, and cyber has no named target. Empty local station/event/fuel queries do not prove safety.
findings.action: Retain direct-versus-indirect, scope, source/effective time and synthetic labels. Add a local event only when source/perimeter/target, units, uncertainty, coverage and NoData are explicit; never promote a zero preset metric to an all-clear.

findings.summary: The complete numerical, checkpoint, allocation, ledger and recovery-accounting contract passes for GM0321.
findings.evidence: The mandatory gate covers ten presets, six checkpoints and eight services. Values are finite/deterministic, zero intensity is exact, local/service totals reconcile, ledgers close, burden is monotone, roads support mobility/supply only and layer selection is invariant.
findings.action: Keep GM0321 and national ALL coverage in regression; add selected-event, hazard-specific ranking, rain-edition, pre-impact evacuation, route-cell, water-service, activity and Unknown-versus-zero assertions.

corrections.summary: Replace generic GM0321 river proximity with an authority-selected, defence-aware Lek event and pre-impact evacuation/action contract.
corrections.validation: Use WMCN LIWO professional releases (national scenario catalogue; 2025.1.6; layer-specific licence/resolution/NoData and expert interpretation required), HDSR Sterke Lekdijk/project data (regional/local segment context; project dates; machine export/licence/cadence must be agreed) and Rijkswaterstaat Waterinfo point observations/forecasts (national point network; generally ten-minute/CC0; public/non-mission-critical) against the full 1,966-position CBS 2025 boundary. Require named river hydrograph/level and datum, defence segment/state, breach/overtopping, probability, connected depth/velocity/arrival/recession grid, effective/issue time, resolution, uncertainty, coverage, NoData and licence. Add warning lead, owner/decision, evacuation zones/routes/destinations, vulnerable assistance, resource/verification and re-entry fields. Until selected, direct local depth/exposure/recovery is Unknown and the scalar is diagnostic only.

corrections.summary: Version and integrate Houten's pluvial/heat surfaces while replacing the shared neighbourhood seed.
corrections.validation: Obtain the municipality's governing 30×30 cm rain raster and model report via the current page https://www.houten.nl/duurzaamheid/klimaatverandering/regenwater or an authorised export. Keep the older 345-location and current 453-location results as separate immutable editions. Record publisher, run/issue date, rainfall hyetograph/return-period climate basis, sewer/surface-water/groundwater assumptions, mitigation baseline, cell/CRS, units, façade/road thresholds, uncertainty, NoData, licence and cadence. Use KNMI Data Platform named radar/observation replays (5-/10-minute, CC BY 4.0) and AHN/BGT only with event alignment. Tests must reject identical full rankings across unrelated hazards and validate known rain/heat areas without treating planning targets as observations.

corrections.summary: Add flood-valid multimodal evacuation, care and supply access while keeping capacity and continuity honest.
corrections.validation: Use RWS NWB OGC/download for national road topology (monthly, CC0 1.0), NDW DATEX II for timestamped current/T+72-valid situations (CC0 unless record/dataset states otherwise), ProRail station/rail geometry (national CC0 snapshots) and OVapi GTFS 9543 (national feed valid 2026-08-30–12-12; free use/best effort/no SLA). Intersect the selected arrival/depth grid with A27/A12/N-roads, local tunnels and rail; add direction, warning/closure time, passability, accessibility, destination/care/shelter role and Unknown capacity. Do not infer passenger flow or guaranteed operation from schedules, and do not add transport routes to utility services.

corrections.summary: Build non-sensitive water-service, utility, communications, facility and activity context without inventing topology or incident occupancy.
corrections.validation: Reconcile HWH Kunstwerken IMWA https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-kunstwerken-imwa/ogc/v2 (national, weekly, CC BY-SA 4.0) and Waterketen DAMO https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-waterketen-damo/ogc/v1 (national, contributor-dependent, CC BY-SA 4.0) with an HDSR/municipal authorised catchment export; register points remain non-causal until connectivity/state/backup is supplied. Mijn Aansluiting WFS is Public Domain provider-responsibility context with provider timestamps, and NBNL is at-least-quarterly/monthly planning context, not outage/load. DUO is daily attribution data, RIVM acute-care v1.1 is fixed CC0 questionnaire context and RDI licence/cadence is unstated. Keep official zero residents separate from business demand; request safe aggregate occupancy, service zones, continuity/backup and restoration bands, leaving unavailable/security-sensitive fields Unknown or explicitly synthetic.

residualLimitations: This audits a deterministic first-72-hour exercise model, not a warning, forecast, hydraulic assessment, evacuation order, outage statement, route guarantee or operator commitment.

CBS 2025 neighbourhood values are rounded/suppressed and sums need not equal the municipality total; null statistics, provider, capacity, monitoring, facility, fuel or forecast fields are Unknown, not zero.
The 71-position overview is suitable for display/selection, not defence, hydraulic, rainfall, sewer, terrain, asset, building or route intersection; use the full 1,966-position geometry.

The 2022 climate-plan flood values are one dated breach scenario and not current probability, live inundation or a universal Houten depth; the one contained LIWO point is a candidate, not an active breach.
The older 345-location and current 453-location T=100 rain results use distinct, incompletely exposed model editions; no governing downloadable raster/version/change log/licence was found.
Waterinfo Culemborg values are timestamped point levels, not dike condition or municipal inundation; T+48/T+72 point absence is NoData and values cannot be aligned silently to synthetic T+0.
HDSR project work and assessments identify safety tasks but not current failure, defence strength, event likelihood, route restriction or dewatering/restoration time.
HWH's 232 objects do not establish connected catchments, live pump/weir/RWZI state, capacity, backup or restoration; contributor completeness varies.
NWB/NDW, ProRail/GTFS, provider territories, NBNL, RDI, DUO and RIVM records do not establish live passability, service continuity, occupancy, physical topology, capacity, backup or repair.

Registered residents and heuristic business demand do not equal people present at business parks, schools, stations, care sites, workplaces, recreation or events; incident-time occupancy is not consumed.

No complete public physical electricity, drinking-water, wastewater, gas, telecom, facility, stock, staffing, backup, repair or restoration topology is consumed; unavailable/security-sensitive gaps remain Unknown or synthetic.
Direct coastal zero, direct-fire zero and event-catalogue no-match are narrow model/query statements and do not mean no indirect coast, vegetation/fire, smoke, seismic, access or supply effect.

Recovery after T+72, pre-impact lead time, cross-boundary dike/service consequences, evacuation destinations, shelter/care capacity, mutual aid, staff/crew and resource constraints remain outside locally validated scope.
